req.title: Return DELETE request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

doc.reasoning: The DELETE /delete endpoint must return HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, and origin. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — plain DELETE with no body returns all required keys with correct types; (2) positive EP — DELETE with JSON body reflects json field correctly; (3) positive EP — DELETE with query string reflects args field; (4) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (GET) on /delete returns 405; (5) boundary BVA — DELETE with empty body yields data='' and json=null; (6) DT — DELETE with form data reflects form field; (7) BVA — all eight required keys present and no extra mutation-detectable values. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant, operator, and key-name mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys
expected: JSON body contains exactly keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010 — view_delete calls get_dict with all 8 keys
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    required_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == required_keys

test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys()

tests.name: test_delete_with_json_body_reflects_json_field
actions: Send DELETE /delete with Content-Type: application/json and body {"key": "value"}
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010 — get_dict parses request.data as JSON into json key
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_json_body_reflects_json_field():
    payload = json.dumps({"key": "value"})
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['json'] == {"key": "value"}
    assert body['data'] == payload

test_delete_with_json_body_reflects_json_field()

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_query_string_reflects_args():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar&baz=qux')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()

tests.name: test_delete_with_form_data_reflects_form_field
actions: Send DELETE /delete with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and field name=alice
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010 — get_dict includes form from request.form; json is None when body is not JSON
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_form_data_reflects_form_field():
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        data={'name': 'alice'},
        content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['form'] == {'name': 'alice'}
    assert body['json'] is None

test_delete_with_form_data_reflects_form_field()

tests.name: test_delete_response_url_contains_delete_path
expected: origin field is a non-empty string
headers field is a non-empty dict
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010 — get_dict populates url via get_url(request), origin via X-Forwarded-For or remote_addr, headers via get_headers()
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_url_contains_delete_path():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert '/delete' in body['url']
    assert isinstance(body['origin'], str)
    assert len(body['origin']) > 0
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert len(body['headers']) > 0

test_delete_response_url_contains_delete_path()

tests.name: test_delete_no_extra_keys_in_response
actions: Send DELETE /delete and inspect response key set exactly
expected: Response JSON has exactly 8 keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin — no more, no less
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010 — view_delete calls get_dict with exactly those 8 keys; mutation of key list would change count or names
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_no_extra_keys_in_response():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == expected_keys
    assert len(body) == 8

test_delete_no_extra_keys_in_response()
